name: Cosmos DB NoSQL Load and Query
description: Create a Cosmos DB database, add a container, bulk-import documents from JSONL, query them back with a NoSQL query, and export the container as clean JSONL.
prerequisites: Workspace on F4+ capacity (Cosmos DB requires F4+)
A JSONL file with one JSON document per line whose field set includes the intended partition key

steps.description: Create the Cosmos DB database item (empty shell; no Azure Cosmos account needed).
steps.notes: Create is a long-running op; the Cosmos database name equals this display name.

steps.description: Create a container. Fabric Cosmos is autoscale-only; fabio sends the autoscale max (--autoscale-max, default 1000 RU/s).
steps.notes: Choose a partition-key path with high cardinality; a leading slash is added if omitted.

steps.description: Bulk-import documents (JSONL, JSON array, or stdin). UPSERT by default (idempotent, retry-safe).
steps.notes: The partition-key value is auto-derived from each document via the container's partition-key path. Add --continue-on-error to skip malformed rows.

steps.command: fabio cosmos-db-database query --workspace $WS_ID --id $COSMOS_ID --container products --query-text "SELECT c.id, c.name, c.currentPrice FROM c WHERE c.currentPrice > @min" --parameter min=100
steps.description: Run a Cosmos NoSQL query. Cross-partition is automatic unless --partition-key is given; --parameter binds @params.
steps.notes: Query text can also be @file or piped via stdin. Use --limit / --all for paging.

steps.description: Export the container as clean JSONL (Cosmos system fields _rid/_self/_etag/_attachments/_ts are stripped so export -> import roundtrips).
steps.notes: Omit --output-file to stream raw JSONL to stdout for piping.

tips: Point-reads/deletes need the partition key: get-document/delete-document require --partition-key (Cosmos has no cross-partition point op).
create-document derives the partition key from the document unless --partition-key is given.
delete-container and delete-document are irreversible; preview with --dry-run first (agents get a destructive agentNotice).
Override the data-plane endpoint with --endpoint only if item-property resolution fails; the endpoint is the item's properties.serverFqdn.
